source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Sterling NVA4 publishes 11 MW of IT capacity, ranking 22nd among the 25 Virginia data centers that disclose any capacity figure at all.

That ranking is the real finding. Virginia has 330 mapped data center facilities, and only 25 of them publish a capacity number. Those 25 total 1,603 MW, and NVA4 holds 0.7% of it. Any state-level capacity total built from published figures is therefore a floor, not a census. For AI specifically, that matters because estimates of where training and inference load can physically land are only as good as the disclosed capacity behind them, and most of Virginia's footprint is undisclosed.

NVA4 itself is a modest asset: 11 MW across 128,715 square feet of technical space, with no certifications published. The reading's estimate of roughly 275 racks follows from assuming 40 kW per rack, which is an assumption about AI training density rather than anything the operator states. At this size the facility sits outside the tier of infrastructure that shapes near-term AI scaling constraints in the state.

What the data does not cover is the part that would decide the facility's future. Grid supply, interconnection queue position, and operator capital plans are all absent, and the suitability score of 57 is derived only from published IT capacity and operator type, with announced expansion listed as missing. The record describes what CyrusOne has disclosed about an existing campus, not what that campus can become.
